races.paceDynamic: Warfleet and Poet's Muse will contest the early lead, with Warfleet making his seasonal debut after 394 days off and Poet's Muse seeking to improve on recent modest efforts. Behind them, prominent runners Limier d'Arthel, Handmedownastar, Docteur Romeo and JPR Two will settle just off the pace, while the bulk of the field including Hardly Surprising, Dutch Corner and Ask A Sainte will be held up. The genuine early gallop created by two willing pace-setters on soft ground will string the field out over this stamina-testing trip. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses — the pace is genuine and the conditions will take their toll on the early leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong between Warfleet and Poet's Muse
scenarios.body: The soft ground and testing distance will find out the prominent runners, allowing the patient hold-up horses to pick up the pieces in the final furlong. Harry Fry's 3/9 strike rate and Dutch Corner's consistent placed form under Dan Skelton make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Limier d'Arthel or Handmedownastar can secure ideal positions behind the leaders
scenarios.body: Philip Hobbs' charge showed promise when second last time and can capitalize if the pace collapses, while Handmedownastar has winning form on similar ground. Their tactical positioning allows them to strike before the hold-up horses get organized.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Warfleet and Poet's Muse fade early leaving no genuine pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where class tells and the better-rated horses can utilize their ability regardless of running style. This neutralizes the tactical advantage and brings the higher-rated runners into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock front-running success
scenarios.trigger: If Warfleet's fresh legs after his long break allow him to sustain his effort
scenarios.body: The combination of his rest and Jimmy Frost getting him fit could see him steal a march on a moderate maiden field. His hurdles experience gives him an edge over some newcomers to the discipline.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Warfleet's fitness after 394 days off - if he blows up early it will collapse the pace scenario completely
Monitor how aggressively Poet's Muse goes early as she may not have the engine to sustain pressure from Warfleet
Check Hardly Surprising's position turning for home - Harry Fry's 33% strike rate suggests this horse is primed for a big run
Observe Limier d'Arthel's jumping under pressure as his fall two runs back suggests he can be sketchy at his hurdles
Watch Dutch Corner's typical hold-up tactics as Dan Skelton's 23% recent record indicates strong stable confidence

races.paceDynamic: Begin The Luck will lead with natural pace-setting instincts, likely joined by Firefly Lane and Devilsrollthedice in the prominent positions early. This creates a moderate but sustainable gallop over the extended 2m5f trip on good to soft ground. The small field of eight allows the pace-setters to dictate without severe pressure, but the genuine staying test will stretch the field in the latter stages. This setup moderately favours hold-up horses who can stay the trip — the pace will be honest enough to set up a finish, and the soft ground adds to the stamina demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Begin The Luck sets steady fractions and the pace builds gradually
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop stretches the field over the final half-mile, allowing the hold-up brigade to pick off tiring leaders. Soft ground emphasizes stamina over speed in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If Begin The Luck gets an easy lead and kicks for home early
scenarios.body: The pace-setter uses tactical speed to steal a march, with prominent runners following through. The small field means less pressure early, allowing front-runners to conserve energy for the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Begin The Luck stops quickly and the early pace proves too strong
scenarios.body: The leaders come back dramatically in the straight, creating a scramble finish. This benefits horses that can quicken from mid-division when the race falls apart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If multiple front-runners engage in early speed battle
scenarios.body: Begin The Luck, Firefly Lane and Devilsrollthedice go too hard early, setting up the race perfectly for closers. The soft ground compounds their effort, making them sitting ducks.

watchPoints.text: Begin The Luck if allowed uncontested lead — natural front-runner could steal significant advantage with tactical riding
Jack's A Legend returning after 311-day break — tongue-tie first time suggests expected improvement but fitness questions remain
Ideallko and Jack Doyen both dropping in class — previous form at higher levels could prove decisive in this company
Firefly Lane and Tractor Jack both show tendency to fade — soft ground may compound their stamina limitations over this trip
Palawan Du Mazet's recent wins came in weak company — step up in class will test whether current form translates

races.paceDynamic: With all seven runners adopting hold-up tactics, this race lacks a natural pace-setter and will likely develop into a tactical crawl. Green Sky showed front-running tendencies in the past and may be forced to make the running by default, but without genuine early pace pressure, the field will bunch up through the early stages. The lack of prominent racers means the tempo will be modest until someone lights the blue touchpaper turning for home. This setup strongly favours horses with the best turn of foot and finishing kick — those who can quickest off the bridle when the race develops late will have a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical crawl benefits finishers
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow with Green Sky reluctantly leading
scenarios.body: The field stays bunched until the home turn where superior finishing speed becomes crucial. Horses with the highest RPR ratings and best recent form will have the edge when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Green Sky dictates throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Green Sky uses his front-running experience to steal a march
scenarios.body: He builds an unassailable lead while the field hesitates behind, making his class advantage count. David Pipe's runner exploits the tactical nature with bold riding from Pritchard.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If no horse takes responsibility early and they crawl
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from two furlongs out where the lightest-weighted horses benefit. Getarose's 20lb weight advantage becomes decisive in a dash to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Even contest suits class
scenarios.trigger: If they go a reasonable gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The superior-rated horses can utilize their ability advantage over the full trip. The race becomes a straightforward test where official ratings prove reliable.

watchPoints.text: Green Sky forced to lead when naturally a hold-up horse could play into rivals' hands if pace becomes too strong
Northern Air making seasonal debut after 94 days off - watch for market confidence and how sharp he appears in preliminaries
Reel Orange wearing tongue-tie for first time - any improvement in jumping fluency could signal gear change working
Early pace development crucial - if they crawl early, look for horses tracking closest to turn into straight
Getarose carrying 20lbs less than top weight - significant advantage if race becomes pure sprint from two furlongs out

races.paceDynamic: Bumpy Evans is the only confirmed front runner in this 8-runner field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a measured gallop that won't stretch his stamina over 2m5f. The six prominent runners (Tahmuras, Scarface, Royal Jewel, Calimystic, Nickelforce, Hardy Du Seuil) will likely settle in a compact group behind the leader, with only Kap Ouest held up in rear. This creates a scenario where the pace may not be strong enough to set up the hold-up horse ideally. This setup moderately favours the prominent runners who can track the moderate pace and have the tactical speed to strike when the race develops in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent runners dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate and the field remains compact into the straight
scenarios.body: The prominent horses will be perfectly positioned to challenge Bumpy Evans and their superior ratings tell. Calimystic and Tahmuras have the class and form to take advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Bumpy Evans gets easy sectionals and quickens clear turning for home
scenarios.body: His 167-day break becomes an asset as fresher legs prevail, while the closers struggle to reel him in on soft ground. Kerry Lee's patient approach with this talented chaser pays dividends.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse strikes late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too hard trying to peg back Bumpy Evans
scenarios.body: Kap Ouest will benefit from a stronger pace as the field strings out down the back straight. His fresh form and hold-up style becomes a decisive weapon in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Nickelforce springs surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the 147-day break has freshened Nickelforce and his low weight tells
scenarios.body: His excellent recent form before the break and 15lb weight advantage could overcome his lower rating. Ben Case's 20% strike rate with his limited runners suggests this horse is ready.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Bumpy Evans shows any signs of rustiness early - the long break could see him caught flat-footed when the pace lifts
Monitor how aggressively the prominent runners position themselves behind Bumpy Evans - if they race keenly it sets up Kap Ouest perfectly
Observe Calimystic's jumping rhythm - his recent wins suggest he's found his form but any jumping errors will compromise his chances
Check if Nickelforce travels smoothly into the race despite the long layoff - his pre-break form suggests he retains plenty of ability
Watch the pace through the middle section - if it becomes truly run this moderate pace could surprise with the finishing kick required

races.paceDynamic: Call Me Legend is the sole confirmed pace-setter and should get an uncontested lead in this small field of eight. With most rivals adopting prominent or hold-up tactics, he'll face minimal early pressure and can dictate terms throughout the 3m2½f trip. The lack of pace pressure means the field will likely travel in a compact group behind the leader until turning for home. This setup moderately favours prominent racers who can track the pace and pounce when Call Me Legend comes under pressure - the genuine gallop will suit those who can stay close without over-racing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend gets soft sectionals and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: His recent wins show he stays well and Philip Hobbs has him in great form. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to conserve energy for a strong finish and hold off late challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend sets steady fractions but weakens in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The patient prominent horses can track the pace without over-exerting and time their challenge perfectly. Crossgales King's recent Newton Abbot win and soft ground form makes him the ideal beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens unexpectedly or Call Me Legend goes too fast early
scenarios.body: Top Guy's excellent soft ground record and Dan Skelton's strong recent form gives him the tactical speed to come from off the pace. His RPR of 122 suggests he has the class edge if getting the right run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend goes very slowly and it becomes a sprint from the last hurdle
scenarios.body: In a bunched finish, class and tactical speed become crucial factors. The race becomes a lottery with any of the field capable of winning in a driving finish.

Rickety Bridge returning from six-week break - his jumping and early enthusiasm will indicate readiness
Sam's Amour having first run for over three months - market support would suggest hidden fitness
